R101.note: Allowlist plus scalar-only check keeps ownerId/_id unoverridable and blocks operator objects, but it silently drops any other criterion the original accepted (e.g. total, items.sku - schema fields) while listing type/priority which are not in the schema, so a legitimate narrowing is ignored and the match is broadened rather than rejected; a non-object extra also now throws outside the try.

R102.note: path.relative(...).startsWith('..') stops '../' escapes, but without a path.isAbsolute(relative) guard a different-drive or UNC path (C:\x, \\server\share\evil) on Windows yields a non-'..' relative and reaches require() - reproduced with Node 24 in scratch - contradicting the write-up's cross-platform claim; legitimate plugin names behave exactly as before.

R103.note: GET replaced by [HttpPost] with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] is the framework-native CSRF fix for a state-changing action, and the required change to the confirmation view (POST form with the token) is stated plainly.

R104.note: Moving param into the filterArgs {0} placeholder lets JNDI escape RFC 4515 metacharacters at the search call, and the search semantics for benign input are unchanged.

R105.note: snprintf into message with a >= sizeof check rejects oversized username:action with -1 instead of overflowing or truncating, and fitting inputs still produce 'AUDIT <username>:<action>' and return 0 exactly as the contract requires.

R106.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param('s')/execute/get_result parameterises the username and the function still returns the first row or null on failure.

R107.note: Column allowlist in the service is the correct shape for a MyBatis ${} ORDER BY sink and keeps #{tenantId}, the created_at default and the listed columns; the stated fallback to created_at for unrecognised values is silent rather than a rejection, which is a mild choice but blocks no contracted use.

R108.note: Extension now derives from the file-type detected MIME via a fixed map, so the client name can never choose it; the resulting normalisation (.jpeg/.JPG -> .jpg) is stated and blocks no legitimate upload.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') on both values at the concatenation point is the right encoder for HTML text context and nothing else changes.

R110.note: channelIndex >= calibrationTable.size() early-return closes the write, matching the function's existing silent-return convention for malformed messages.

R111.note: Replacing hand-built docmd envelope commands with sendmail() routes both addresses through smtplib's mail()/rcpt(), whose putcmd raises ValueError on any CR/LF (reproduced with CPython 3.13 in scratch) and dot-stuffs the DATA body; the only difference is that relay refusals now raise instead of being ignored.

R112.note: id = ANY($1::int[]) with the array as a bound parameter is the idiomatic node-pg replacement for a hand-built IN list and returns the same rows; the explicit ::int[] cast assumes an int4 id column, which the write-up states.

R113.note: pathinfo(PATHINFO_EXTENSION) checks only the final extension, and the stated switch to a hash-based stored name (dropping the original filename the comment wanted kept) is extra hardening that blocks no legitimate upload.

R114.note: resize(count) fixes the out-of-bounds write into packet, but the same untrusted count still indexes fields[i] past its size for count > fields.size(), and the contract's requirement to reject or report an oversized count is not met; behaviour for valid counts is preserved.

R115.note: @PreAuthorize('hasRole(ADMIN)') on processMonthEndCleanup is enforced on the proxied call from the controller, closing the self-invocation bypass at the entry point; the case's own comments establish that non-admin access to this path was never intended, so the restriction is the contract.

R116.note: Arrow-function callback passes reminderId and message as values, so no request data is ever evaluated as source text, and the logged entry is identical for legitimate input.

R117.note: res.sendFile(name, { root }) makes send treat the name as relative and reject '..' segments with 403, which is Express's own containment mechanism; legitimate report names resolve to the same files as before.
